override.reason: (1) This IS the de-duplicated form, not the smell: the shared override-then-derive logic lives once in _telemetry_path, and the three wrappers are named seams over it. Deleting them pushes two magic strings per channel back to every call site and drops each channel's recorded contract, so complexity reappears across callers -- the deletion test says they earn their keep. (2) Merging the two refusal texts would undo the fix. _unbound_refusal's docstring records why they must stay apart: an unbound door has no path to name, so one message that promises to name a path is unsatisfiable there and invites a fabricated path. I reproduced that distinction as a fact of the code, not just the prose -- the unbound branch names no path, the named-but-unusable branch does. Merging re-merges the two refusal classes whose separation is what #603 bought.

The gate's real design smell, and it is evidenced by the gate's own blocker history rather than by taste. ONE fact -- when and how the door acquires identity -- is restated as unchecked prose across many sites. Measured, not estimated: an AST-and-comment sweep over scripts/ tests/ docs/ examples/ for prose co-mentioning binding and spine_open/_bind_process_to returns 23 distinct sites (12 in scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, 9 across four test modules, 2 in docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md); that count is an upper bound because it also catches refusal-message text and test names, and the tighter set of true restatements a prior reviewer identified is about seven. Either way the consequence is measured: THREE of this gate's four rework cycles were a restatement that had drifted from the code (blocker 2, the pin's failure message; blocker 3, four further claims; and my own r5 finding on docs/CHECKLIST_ENGINE_DESIGN.md, a fourth). Only two of these sites are mechanically tied to the code (the AST pins in tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py); the rest can drift silently, and repeatedly have. Already filed as a triage candidate by a prior reviewer and acknowledged in the handoff as a design change beyond this gate -- I concur it is out of scope to fix here, and record it flagged rather than overridden because no repo standard sanctions it: CREW_CONTEXT.md's own verification discipline ('assert against behaviour, never against text that describes it') points the other way.

scripts/mcp_spine_server.py changed for exactly one reason in this gate -- how the door acquires and refuses identity. The telemetry accessors it also touched are the same concern (a destination derived from the bound spine), not a second axis of change.

No caller walks a chain of intermediaries. The longest expressions are Path(...).resolve().parent and common.resolve().parent inside _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle -- pathlib value operations on one object, not a chain that couples the caller to a graph of collaborators.

_telemetry_path(env_var, beside_the_spine) is the only generalization added, and it has three real callers today (_calllog, _start_marker, _rejectionlog), so it is extracted from duplication rather than anticipating it. BINDS_WITHOUT_A_BOUND_SPINE is a one-element set, which reads speculative, but it is the live predicate the unbound-refusal branch tests against and naming it is what makes that exemption greppable rather than an inline string compare. No unused hook, parameter or abstract seam was added.

scripts/mcp_spine_server.py's module docstring is 143 lines and several added function docstrings run 30-60 lines, far past what a reader needs to call them. On its face that is prose compensating for code.
